name: Denver, Colorado, 1 June 2015 (evening balloon)
line: Dry air near the ground and cloud bases over 2 km up, moderate instability (CAPE about 1300 J/kg) and strong wind shear (24 m/s over 6 km): high-based storms with little rain.
note: The balloon launched at 0000 UTC on 2 June (6 pm local time on the 1st). Picked by a stated rule (dry, high cloud base, moderate instability, strong shear) from Great Plains evening balloons. The storm is started by a gentle push of rising air, as CM1's updraft nudging does. In a 1 km run the storm stays weak, with little rain, and is gone within about 45 minutes (measured). This day's sounding in an idealized storm, not a reconstruction of that day's storms.

gm1_settings_why: The push of rising air that starts the storm is centred 0.1 km east and 6.5 km south of the centre, the storm-track check's recommended place for this sounding, so the storm keeps the most room to every side. CM1 keeps the nudging's centre in its code (xc_wnudge, yc_wnudge), not the namelist, so this is a GM1 setting.
